payload.claim: The warning text asserts the log "stopped accepting writes", but `EventLog.failed` is a one-time latch (set to `True` on the first caught exception and never reset), and `append` does not gate itself on that flag — a later call can and does still write successfully. `tests/test_task.py`'s own criterion-3 test proves this: after the synthetic first-append failure, `read_log(out_dir / "SY-10") == events` shows every subsequent event was in fact written, yet the terminal still reports the log as having stopped. An operator reading this line for a night with a single transient write hiccup (e.g. a momentarily full disk that then frees space) will be told the log stopped when it did not, which is exactly the kind of misdiagnosis this spec exists to prevent.
